steps: 1. Record the plan and contract first (docs only). Create docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-implementation-plan.md from this step list (it follows the July design-plan docs/plans/2026-07-13-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-design-plan.md, whose Task 1 characterization tests already exist). Add a 'Checksum-compatible resume projection integrity' section to specs/state.md that covers: audit order (CLI, root executor, reached call); explicit-identity versus omitted-step_id compatibility; the four repeat_until progress forms and the for_each rules; call-frame and Workflow Lisp retry lineage; the checksum and projection failure envelopes (status/error/updated_at only); the sticky non-routable failure with supplemental finalization; the diagnostic v1 shape with its twelve reasons and privacy rules; no receipts or caches; and schema staying "2.1". Add matching positive and negative acceptance entries to specs/acceptance/index.md, each pointing to the test module that will prove it (steps 2-13). Touches: docs/plans/2026-10-18-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-implementation-plan.md, specs/state.md, specs/acceptance/index.md.

2. Typed Workflow Lisp provenance (item 8), TDD. RED tests: (a) every bundle from compile_stage3_entrypoint has provenance.frontend_kind == 'workflow_lisp': the validated bundles, imported Workflow Lisp bundles reached through imports, and lowered bundles; (b) a classic-YAML bundle passed through imported_workflow_bundles keeps frontend_kind None and is linked as the same object; (c) build_frontend_bundle keeps the kind the compiler set; (d) CallExecutor._is_workflow_lisp_target is true exactly for frontend_kind == 'workflow_lisp', so a .orc path without the kind is false and a non-.orc path with the kind is true. GREEN: set frontend_kind where the compiler builds or lowers bundles. Stop passing frontend_kind="workflow_lisp" in the replace() call in build_frontend_bundle (the kind is inherited from the bundle). Make _is_workflow_lisp_target read provenance.frontend_kind instead of the .orc suffix. Touches: orchestrator/workflow_lisp/compiler.py, orchestrator/workflow_lisp/build.py (and orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/* only if lowered bundles are rebuilt there), orchestrator/workflow/calls.py (_is_workflow_lisp_target), tests/test_workflow_lisp_build_artifacts.py, tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py.

3. Classic-YAML duplicate import aliases before bundle construction (item 5), TDD. RED tests through WorkflowLoader.load, each asserting WorkflowValidationError and that orchestrator.loader.build_loaded_workflow_bundle is never called (substitute the module name): duplicate keys inside imports; a '<<' merge inside imports that repeats an alias; repeated top-level imports sections; top-level '<<' merge sources that each carry imports. Each must yield exactly one 'imports.<alias>: duplicate import alias' naming every occurrence as 'line L, column C' (1-based, the alias key). Distinct aliases across repeated sections yield exactly one 'imports: duplicate top-level mapping' naming each imports key, and no alias error. A single merged imports section with unique aliases still loads. GREEN: add a small node-level scan in a new module orchestrator/loader_import_aliases.py (loader.py is already over 6000 lines). It composes the YAML document with the PreservingLoader resolvers, walks the top-level mapping and its '<<' merge sources to collect imports key nodes and alias key nodes with start_mark line/column + 1, and returns error strings. Call it from WorkflowLoader._load_workflow before the yaml.load result is turned into imports and before _load_imports/build_loaded_workflow_bundle, reporting through the existing _add_error/_raise_validation_errors path. Touches: orchestrator/loader_import_aliases.py (new), orchestrator/loader.py, tests/test_loader_validation.py.

4. Projection resume API: boundary alias and slot enumeration, TDD. RED tests on generated workflows. CallBoundaryProjection gains import_alias (keyword-constructible) and lowering fills it with the authored call alias. WorkflowStateProjection.enumerate_resume_slots(state) returns a ResumeProjectionSlotIndex holding candidates_by_step_id (root, finalization and loop-local candidates with node_id, region and iteration_index, built only through the existing IterationStepKeyProjection.runtime_step_id/step_key and CallBoundaryProjection.runtime_step_id APIs), call_boundaries_by_step_id (loop-contained boundaries expanded per iteration through call_boundary_runtime_step_id), and unclaimed_explicit_rows (each step_id snapshotted as persisted, including unhashable values). It never mutates or backfills state. Also: resolve_resume_step_id(slot_index, step_id, presentation_key=None) returns slot, candidate_count and exact_identity_candidate_count, and malformed or unhashable ids resolve to 0 candidates instead of raising. resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id) returns boundary and candidate_count. ResumeProjectionValidationError(ValueError) carries .reason and .message, and str() equals the message. GREEN: keep the dataclasses and thin delegating methods in state_projection.py, and put the enumeration and resolution logic in a new orchestrator/workflow/resume_slot_index.py so both files stay under 500 lines. No string splitting, prefix matching or reconstruction of ids. Touches: orchestrator/workflow/state_projection.py, orchestrator/workflow/resume_slot_index.py (new), orchestrator/workflow/lowering.py (CallBoundaryProjection construction near line 180), tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py.

5. Loop bookkeeping validation inside enumerate_resume_slots (item 3), TDD. RED: a parametrized table on a for_each named ProcessItems and a repeat_until named ReviewLoop asserting the exact reason and message pairs from the interface list (8 unsupported_shape, 10 invalid_loop_progress). Positive cases: the four admitted repeat_until forms are active; terminal condition success; terminal successful exhaustion with completed on_exhausted outputs and a completed loop step; terminal failed exhaustion with a failed loop step whose error.type is repeat_until_iterations_exhausted. Also valid for_each progress with and without current_index. Booleans are never accepted as indices. Then show that valid bookkeeping still yields 0 candidates for a stale loop-local step id or loop-contained boundary id. GREEN: a pure validator in a new orchestrator/workflow/resume_loop_progress.py, called by resume_slot_index.py before loop-local candidates are expanded. It reads the declared maximum from the projection or loop config only, and touches no files or checksums. Touches: orchestrator/workflow/resume_loop_progress.py (new), orchestrator/workflow/resume_slot_index.py, tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py.

6. Retry-lineage indexing (item 4, pure), TDD. RED unit tests for index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind) and next_unused_retry_frame_id: a base B with retries B::retry::n; completed members unlimited and never resumable; failed_predecessors in ordinal order; zero or one running_member. Failure cases: mixed bases, two running members, a duplicate ordinal, or several non-completed frames of a non-Workflow-Lisp boundary give ambiguous_resumable_call_frame; a missing or malformed ordinal, a nested '::retry::' marker or an unknown status give unsupported_shape; a call_step_id other than the boundary gives missing_call_boundary; differing aliases give persisted_import_alias_mismatch. The result is independent of mapping order. The next id is the lowest unused positive ordinal over all members including completed ones, and repeated calls return the same id. GREEN: a new orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_retry_lineage.py holding CallFrameRetryLineage, RetryFrameMember, CallFrameRetryLineageError(ValueError, .reason), index_retry_lineage and next_unused_retry_frame_id, re-exported from resume_projection_integrity in step 7. Touches: orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_retry_lineage.py (new), tests/test_call_frame_retry_lineage.py (new).

7. Scope auditor module, TDD. RED tests in a new tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py. ResumeScopePath: frozen; root(); child() snapshots the frame ids to a tuple; projection_scope; as_context(). audit_scope(bundle, state, scope_path) cases: a valid root passes; a state with no step_id passes and is not backfilled (deep-equal before and after); and one case per reason (all twelve) asserting the full v1 diagnostic. The diagnostic has type resume_projection_integrity_error, message 'Resume projection integrity audit failed: <reason>', diagnostic_schema, reason, scope_path, field, offending_value (null for containers), expected_owner {workflow_file, workflow_checksum, projection_scope}, candidate_count and call_boundary_step_id, all always present. The cases cover steps, current_step.step_id (mandatory), call_frames.<id>.call_step_id/import_alias/position, call_frames and steps that are not mappings, and an import missing from bundle.imports. Privacy tests plant sentinel secrets in bound_inputs, context, artifacts and frame state, plus a malformed list or dict used as an id, and assert none of them appears in json.dumps(error). Architecture tests on the module source check: no import of migration_parity or procedure_identity_retirement, no load_parity_targets, load_retirement_evidence, load_retirement_record or validate_retirement_record, no 'receipt', and no 'cache' together with audit, resume projection or projection integrity; patching builtins.open, Path.read_text, the loaders and StateManager.calculate_checksum to raise does not break audit_scope. GREEN: a new orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py defining ResumeScopePath, ResumeProjectionIntegrityError(ValueError, .error), a single _diagnostic builder and audit_scope. audit_scope uses bundle.projection with enumerate_resume_slots, resolve_resume_step_id and resolve_call_boundary, and index_retry_lineage per boundary to group frames. It audits only the given scope (recursion into frames happens at reached calls, step 11) and re-exports the lineage API. Keep it under 500 lines. Touches: orchestrator/workflow/resume_projection_integrity.py (new), tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py (new).

8. StateManager failure envelopes, TDD. RED tests in tests/test_state_manager.py. record_workflow_checksum_mismatch(*, workflow_file, persisted_checksum, current_checksum, reason) writes error = {type: workflow_checksum_mismatch, message: 'Workflow has been modified since the run started', context: {workflow_file, persisted_checksum, current_checksum, reason}}. The first three values are str or null, and reason must be one of workflow_modified, missing_recorded_checksum, missing_workflow_path or workflow_unavailable (anything else raises ValueError). record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(error) persists the given diagnostic. Both set status to failed and refresh updated_at atomically (through the existing _write_json_atomic path), leave unknown root fields, steps, current_step, call_frames and the run tree byte-identical apart from those three fields, and do not call fail_run (assert by substituting it). GREEN: two small methods on StateManager that read the raw state.json dict, change the three keys and write atomically. Touches: orchestrator/state.py, tests/test_state_manager.py.

9. Resume CLI root audit and ordering (item 1, CLI half), TDD. RED tests in tests/test_resume_command.py that substitute orchestrator.cli.commands.resume.audit_scope, _merge_observability_overrides, open_executor_session and WorkflowExecutor to record order. They assert: the existing checksum precheck still fails first with exit 1 and nothing written; audit_scope runs after schema and checksum acceptance with ResumeScopePath.root(<workflow_file>) and before overrides, session or process metadata, executor construction and prologue. An audit failure exits 1, prints the reason to stderr, persists only the status/error/updated_at delta (run tree snapshot diff), and opens no session or process metadata. Update the Task-1 characterization tests that pinned the old gap (test_projection_resume_integrity_mutation_order_cli_root_explicit_id_corruption, test_resume_fails_closed_on_projection_current_step_integrity_mismatch) to the new contract rather than deleting them. GREEN: add 'from orchestrator.workflow.resume_projection_integrity import ResumeProjectionIntegrityError, ResumeScopePath, audit_scope' as module-level names in resume.py, then call audit_scope(bundle, state_dict, ...) right after the validate_checksum block (around line 466) and before any override merge or open_executor_session. On ResumeProjectionIntegrityError call state_manager.record_resume_projection_integrity_failure(exc.error), print to stderr and return 1. Touches: orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, tests/test_resume_command.py.

10. Structural-root executor guard (items 1 and 6), TDD. RED tests in tests/test_resume_command.py (direct WorkflowExecutor.execute(resume=True)), substituting orchestrator.workflow.executor.audit_scope and StateManager.calculate_checksum. Checksum cases: a changed file gives workflow_modified; no recorded checksum gives missing_recorded_checksum; no workflow path gives missing_workflow_path; an unreadable file gives workflow_unavailable. Each persists only the checksum envelope, makes no audit call and does not run the prologue (substitute _execute_prologue). A checksum-compatible identity change made after the CLI audit passed is caught by the second root audit: three-field delta, existing session and process metadata kept, prologue not run, and the CLI's close_executor_session marks the session failed without replacing the error, even when the close itself raises. A child call-frame executor (state_manager has a str frame_id, the existing is_call_frame test near line 2474) skips the root guard. GREEN: add a module-level audit_scope import and a _resume_root_guard(state) in executor.py, called at the top of execute() before _execute_prologue when resume and not a call frame. It computes the checksum with self.state_manager.calculate_checksum and then calls audit_scope with ResumeScopePath.root. If executor.py would grow materially, move the guard body into a new orchestrator/workflow/resume_root_guard.py and keep a thin call site. Adjust the resume.py finally/close path so the session close status is failed and the persisted error is never overwritten. Touches: orchestrator/workflow/executor.py, orchestrator/workflow/resume_root_guard.py (new, optional), orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py, orchestrator/runtime_observability.py (only if close_executor_session needs a preserve-error path), tests/test_resume_command.py.

11. Reached-call revalidation and retry lineage at execute_call (item 4), TDD. RED integration tests in tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py using generic two- and three-level YAML and Workflow Lisp import fixtures that substitute orchestrator.workflow.calls.audit_scope and record calls of WorkflowStateProjection.resolve_call_boundary. They assert: exactly one resolve_call_boundary(slot_index, call_step_id) call per reached call identity, made positionally; it runs after the parent call visit/start publication and after authored, managed/runtime input, write-root, checksum and resume-bound-input validation, but before any child StateManager or executor is created or changed. The boundary's current import_alias selects the callee and a persisted alias mismatch fails. A completed frame whose id collides with the target frame id raises the existing call_resume_state_invalid contract violation with detail completed_call_frame_id_collision, whatever its call_step_id (matching, stale or missing); no child manager is created and frames are unchanged. Lineage order: with a running member, its call_resume_checksum_mismatch or bound-input failure wins, then each failed predecessor is checksum-checked and audited with scope_path.child(id) in ordinal order, then the running member is audited and resumed. Without one, all failed predecessors are validated and audited before next_unused_retry_frame_id allocates the new frame. Nested scopes recurse the same way. Flip the Task-1 gap tests (stale_caller_id_starts_fresh_child, mutation_order_callee_local_corruption, ambiguity_is_an_explicit_feasibility_prerequisite) to the new fail-closed behaviour. GREEN: move the selection and lineage logic into a new orchestrator/workflow/call_resume_guard.py, which replaces _retry_frame_id, _retry_family_base and _is_failed_retry_family_frame in calls.py with index_retry_lineage and next_unused_retry_frame_id. calls.py imports audit_scope at module level and calls it through that name. Thread the child ResumeScopePath to the child executor (the constructor or call runtime near executor.py:8209) so nested calls extend the path. Touches: orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, orchestrator/workflow/call_resume_guard.py (new), orchestrator/workflow/call_frame_state.py, orchestrator/workflow/executor.py (child scope path plumbing), tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py.

12. Failure propagation, stickiness and finalization (item 6), TDD. RED tests in a new tests/test_resume_projection_failure_routing.py. A reached-callee audit failure becomes the caller's failed call-step result and the scope/run error, never wrapped in call_failed; the selected callee frame and state stay byte-identical; ancestor frames persist ordinary failed step, current, visit and frame snapshots; the identical diagnostic reaches the root. Authored success, failure and always routes, on_error=continue and for_each/repeat_until continuation all stop (_handle_control_flow returns '_stop'; no next iteration). Configured finalization still runs. A cleanup failure is recorded as finalization.status failed with failure {step, step_id, error: <projection error or null>} and never replaces the run error. A projection error raised only inside finalization becomes both the run error and finalization.failure.error. The epilogue and session close preserve the error. GREEN: in executor.py, _handle_control_flow checks error.type == 'resume_projection_integrity_error' before the cycle-guard, goto and on_error branches and returns '_stop'. Make the call-step failure path in calls.py and the child-result promotion in executor.py pass the diagnostic through unchanged. Add the same short-circuit to the loop continuation decisions in loops.py. Record the supplemental failure in finalization.py (record_step_result / record_settled_result) and keep the run error in _execute_epilogue. Touches: orchestrator/workflow/executor.py, orchestrator/workflow/calls.py, orchestrator/workflow/loops.py, orchestrator/workflow/finalization.py, orchestrator/workflow/outcomes.py (only if routing outcomes are derived there), tests/test_resume_projection_failure_routing.py (new).

13. Forensic current_step in observability (item 6), TDD. RED tests. When the run error type is resume_projection_integrity_error or workflow_checksum_mismatch and current_step is unchanged, build_status_snapshot reports the run as failed with that error and shows that step as pending: status and summary 'pending', current_visit_count null, counted under pending and not running. render_status_markdown never says 'in progress' for it. The stale-heartbeat interpretation (derive_status_projection), the monitor classifier and the dashboard projection do not treat it as live or stalled. GREEN: one shared predicate, e.g. a _forensic_current_step(state) in report.py, reused by the monitor and dashboard rather than reimplemented. Touches: orchestrator/observability/report.py, orchestrator/monitor/classifier.py, orchestrator/dashboard/projection.py, tests/test_observability_report.py, tests/test_dashboard_projection.py, plus the monitor classifier test module.

14. Verification and routing. Run pytest --collect-only -q on every new or renamed test module (tests/test_resume_projection_integrity.py, tests/test_call_frame_retry_lineage.py, tests/test_resume_projection_failure_routing.py). Then run the focused selectors: tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py, tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py, tests/test_resume_command.py, tests/test_state_manager.py, tests/test_loader_validation.py, tests/test_workflow_lisp_build_artifacts.py, tests/test_observability_report.py and tests/test_dashboard_projection.py. Run an orchestrator resume smoke check: start an example workflow, interrupt it, run 'orchestrator resume <run_id>' once on an unchanged checksum-compatible state (resumes) and once with a corrupted step_id (exit 1, three-field delta). Finally run the broad suite 'pytest -q -n 16 --dist=worksteal' in tmux and record fresh output. Update docs/capability_status_matrix.md and docs/index.md to mark the hardening implemented and route to the specs/state.md section. Mark the July design plan's runtime handoff complete in docs/plans/2026-07-13-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-design-plan.md. Confirm the schema version is still "2.1" and that no receipt or cache artifact was added. Commit each green step (2-13) separately. Touches: docs/capability_status_matrix.md, docs/index.md, docs/plans/2026-07-13-resume-projection-integrity-hardening-design-plan.md.

findings: P1 — Steps 1 and 14 skip the repository's prerequisite design gate. docs/design/resume_projection_integrity_hardening.md and the July implementation plan do not exist, specs/state.md and the acceptance index still describe the gap, and docs/design/README.md calls the July design/planning plan the current selector. The proposed plan invents the insertion, diagnostic and state contracts before the accepted target design/reviews required by that selector, then marks its handoff complete. Complete or explicitly supersede that gate first; the referenced 'twelve reasons' and exact loop reason/message interface are not actually defined in a checked-in authority.

P1 — Step 9's CLI insertion point cannot meet its own ordering test. orchestrator/cli/commands/resume.py persists _merge_observability_overrides via _write_state before workflow load and validate_checksum. Calling audit_scope after validate_checksum still permits a checksum mismatch or integrity failure to change observability and updated_at, and fails the existing byte-identical changed-source contract. Move the override merge/write after both prechecks and test with nondefault override flags.

P1 — Steps 8 and 10 change the existing root checksum contract outside the checksum-compatible hardening scope. specs/state.md and acceptance item 197 require a changed root checksum to reject before executor construction with the entire run tree byte-identical. The proposed record_workflow_checksum_mismatch writes status/error/updated_at for direct-executor mismatches and the new state clause would apparently normalize that change. Preserve the current checksum behavior or obtain an explicit contract change; test CLI and direct executor separately.

P1 — Step 11 puts parent-boundary resolution too late. CallExecutor.execute_call currently selects imported_bundle from the authored alias, resolves bindings, chooses a frame, then checks write roots, callee checksum and bound inputs. A corrupt persisted call_step_id/import_alias can therefore trigger the wrong callee's validation or an existing contract error before the promised resume_projection_integrity_error; the proposed GREEN text only adds a guard after those validations. Resolve the current parent call boundary and compare its alias before selecting the callee, then preserve the required checksum/bound-input precedence for the selected existing frame.

P1 — Step 11 explicitly audits reached calls after parent call visit/start publication, conflicting with the intended 'before any mutation or effect' guarantee; its failure tests even require ancestor visit/current/frame snapshots to change. State whether that guarantee is per callee scope, or move the reached-call validation ahead of parent publication. Otherwise a corrupt persisted frame can mutate the run before it is rejected.

P1 — Steps 6 and 11 treat a boundary's retry frames as one family without separating legitimate visits or ancestor retries. frame_id_with_overrides embeds visit_count and prefixes nested IDs with the parent frame ID; a repeated call boundary can have multiple completed visit bases, and a nested call under a retried parent already contains '::retry::' in its prefix. The proposed mixed-base/nested-marker rejection or global marker parsing can reject valid Workflow Lisp resumes, or choose the wrong frame. Key lineage to the exact reached visit and scope; add repeated-visit and nested-retry integration cases.

P1 — Step 12's propagation sketch misses exception handling that can replace the diagnostic. WorkflowExecutor._execute_step_loop catches all Exception, calls fail_run with _executor_exception_error, then re-raises; CLI's broad except and finally also update/write state. ResumeProjectionIntegrityError is a ValueError, so an audit raised inside a call or finalization can become an executor error or call_failed rather than the required stable error. Specify one result/exception propagation path through these handlers and prove the persisted root diagnostic survives epilogue and session close.

P1 — Steps 8 and 10 leave StateManager's in-memory RunState stale after raw JSON failure writes. The proposed methods read/write state.json directly, but CLI finally closes the session by mutating state_manager.state and calling _write_state, which serializes that stale object and can erase the integrity error and unknown root fields. Reload/synchronize before any later write, and explicitly reconcile the claimed three-field delta with the required executor-session close update, including a close failure.

P2 — Step 7's privacy tests omit attacker-controlled identity strings and keys. The proposed diagnostic always includes offending_value, scope_path, field and workflow_file; a malformed step_id, call-frame key or import alias can itself contain a secret or be arbitrarily long, so merely nulling containers and planting secrets in unrelated payloads does not establish a privacy bound. Define length, character and redaction/hash rules for every persisted value rendered in the v1 diagnostic and test those identity fields directly.

P2 — Steps 4, 5 and 7 do not state how the auditor traverses the duplicate loop-result representations. orchestrator/workflow/loops.py stores for_each results as a list at steps.<loop> and again as indexed steps.<loop>[i].<nested>; repeat_until also stores frame and nested rows. An implementation that assumes every steps value is a mapping, or audits only indexed rows, can reject valid runs or miss a corrupted explicit ID in the other persisted copy. Specify and test both forms, including mismatched copies, while retaining the omitted-step_id compatibility lane.

P2 — Step 3's node scan needs recursive YAML merge semantics and an immediate abort before import loading. The specified walk of top-level mapping and its merge sources does not cover nested merge chains or aliases reused through merge sequences; _load_workflow currently calls _load_imports before its final validation raise, and that path builds child bundles. Include recursive/cyclic merge handling and ensure a detected duplicate raises before _load_imports, with tests that assert no bundle is built anywhere in the import graph.

steps: 1. Design gate first: finish the July design-and-planning plan's Task 2 before any contract or code (fixes the skipped prerequisite gate). Prerequisite check: the July Task 1 characterization tests already exist at commit 1cd6076 (tests/test_resume_command.py: test_resume_fails_closed_on_projection_current_step_integrity_mismatch, test_projection_resume_integrity_mutation_order_cli_root_explicit_id_corruption, test_projection_resume_integrity_mutation_order_direct_executor_root_explicit_id_corruption; tests/test_subworkflow_calls.py: ..._ambiguity_is_an_explicit_feasibility_prerequisite, ..._stale_caller_id_starts_fresh_child, ..._callee_local_corruption_updates_parent_and_child; tests/test_workflow_state_projection.py: test_projection_resume_integrity_*). Run them with the July Task 1 selector and record the output. Create docs/design/resume_projection_integrity_hardening.md from docs/templates/design_template.md. The task contract (items 1-8 and the public interface) is the design input. The design compares the four insertion architectures the July plan names (CLI pre-executor, executor prologue, planner-owned, split root/call-boundary) and selects split root (CLI plus structural-root executor) with reached-call audits. It must define, as checked-in authority, the twelve v1 reasons with field/offending_value/candidate_count, and the full loop reason/message table (8 unsupported_shape, 10 invalid_loop_progress). It must also settle these decisions raised in review: (a) CLI order: load -> lowering-schema check -> root checksum precheck -> root audit -> persist observability overrides -> session/process metadata -> executor construction -> prologue. The override merge stays a pure computation but its state write moves after both prechecks (step 11). (b) Checksum contract: the CLI precheck and acceptance item 197 (reject before WorkflowExecutor construction, run tree byte-identical) are unchanged. The executor-recheck envelope (item 6) is an explicit, scoped contract amendment that the task requests. It applies only when a structurally root WorkflowExecutor first sees the mismatch: direct library resume, or a source change between the CLI precheck and the prologue. The design names it as a change to the checksum contract and states that 197/198 are not weakened. (c) Mutation guarantee is per failing scope. Root-scope corruption, including root call frames' call_step_id, import_alias and lineage shape, is rejected by the CLI audit with zero mutation (plus the item-6 three-field envelope). Callee-scope corruption is found at the reached call, after the parent's ordinary visit/start publication. The only allowed delta is the parent's ordinary failed call-step/current/visit/ancestor-frame snapshots plus the promoted error. The selected callee's frame and state stay untouched and no callee effect runs. The purpose statement is restated as 'before any mutation or effect in the failing scope'. (d) Reached-call order: resolve the boundary, then select the bundle by the boundary's current alias, then check target-frame collision, then index the lineage. All of this precedes binding resolution, write-root, callee checksum and bound-input validation, because callee selection depends on it. Then the running member's call_resume_checksum_mismatch and resume-bound-input validation, which win over callee-scope audits. Then each failed predecessor's checksum and audit in ordinal order. Then the running member's audit. Then child StateManager/executor creation. (e) Lineage key: (scope, boundary call_step_id, reached visit base). The base is the fresh-path frame id '<parent frame prefix>.<step_id>::visit::<n>' that frame_id_with_overrides builds. A retry marker is recognised only after the final '::visit::<n>' segment, so a parent prefix that contains '::retry::' is legitimate. Lineages of earlier visits of the same boundary are historical: their shape is audited but they are never resumed. 'At most one non-completed frame per boundary' (classic) and 'one retry lineage per boundary' (Workflow Lisp) are both read per reached visit. At most one visit lineage of a boundary in a scope may hold a running member. Visit-keyed retry lineage (item 4, pure), TDD. index_retry_lineage(boundary_step_id, frame_items, *, frontend_kind) indexes one lineage: the frames of one reached visit base in one scope, as the accepted design defines. A retry marker '::retry::<n>' is recognised only after the frame id's final '::visit::<n>' segment, so ids like 'P::visit::1::retry::1.S::visit::1::retry::2' (a nested call under a retried parent) are valid members with ordinal 2 and base 'P::visit::1::retry::1.S::visit::1'.
